classification.difficultyReason: Infer the outer radius from the radial thickness, subtract sector areas and identify both arcs plus the two short straight edges as the shaded boundary.

inlines.text: The following region is made from two sectors
Find the area and perimeter of the shaded region.

spec.description: Concentric sectors centred at O, with P, A and O collinear and O, B and Q collinear. Both arcs lie above O. Single ticks mark OA and OB; double ticks mark AP and BQ. Dimensions 4 and 8 lie below the left radius.
spec.mathematics: The common central angle is 150 degrees. OA=OB=8 cm and AP=BQ=4 cm. The diagram uses proportional drawing radii 2 and 3 for mathematical radii 8 cm and 12 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the target-region shading are visible; the outer radius, area and perimeter are not supplied.

answer.short:
$A=\dfrac{100\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2$, $P=8+\dfrac{50\pi}{3}\text{ cm}$.

Subtract the inner sector area from the outer sector area. The perimeter includes both arcs and the two straight edges.
answer.worked:
Convert the central angle to radians:
$$\begin{align*}
\theta&=150^\circ\times\frac{\pi}{180^\circ}\\
\theta&=\frac{5\pi}{6}.
\end{align*}$$
The outer radius is $OP=8+4=12\text{ cm}$.

Subtract the sector areas:
$$\begin{align*}
A&=\frac12(12^2-8^2)\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)\\
A&=\frac{100\pi}{3}\text{ cm}^2.
\end{align*}$$
The boundary contains both arcs and two straight edges of length $4\text{ cm}$:
$$\begin{align*}
P&=12\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)+8\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)+4+4\\
P&=8+\frac{50\pi}{3}\text{ cm}.
\end{align*}$$
